units: Defines objects for adaptive authority dynamics: mechanisms, authority weights, residuals, attribution, and viability outcomes.
m_i=(x_i,phi_i,A_i); computational structure with functional contribution and authority weight.
M_t is the active mechanism set and may change through creation, removal, merging, splitting, or representation expansion.
A_i(t) is proposed measurable causal influence, distinct from confidence, probability, reward, and correctness.
mathcal A_t is the distribution of authority across mechanisms.
e_t=y_t-yhat_t is the observed discrepancy driving redistribution pressure.
Phi_R:E x M -> R+ assigns responsibility to a mechanism for residual evidence.
beta controls responsiveness to contradiction and trades faster correction against instability risk.
A_(i,t+1)=A_(i,t) exp[-beta Phi_R(e_t,m_i)] is the proposed decay rule.
n_(1/2)=ln(2)/(beta Phi_R) under constant residual pressure.
Recovery requires positive changes in grounded reachability and correction capacity.
Delta V denotes improved accessible futures, correction ability, and robustness under change.
Failure drives residual-attribution-authority loss; success plus viability gain drives recovery.
Authority landscapes evolve under empirical pressure; central claim is alignment of influence with viable mechanisms.
The source specifies desired attribution properties but not a validated estimator for Phi_R.
The source defines authority as measurable causal influence but does not provide an identification procedure establishing a weight as causal control.
Operational estimators for accessible futures, correction ability, and robustness are not specified here.
Fourteen axioms specify constraints the source claims are required for stable adaptive authority dynamics.
Authority is time-dependent and changes through empirical interaction.
Attributed contradiction must reduce responsible mechanism authority.
Authority updates must be conditioned on mechanism-level attribution rather than residual magnitude alone.
Authority attenuation is proposed as multiplicative exponential dynamics.
Decay is direct after contradiction while restoration requires accumulated evidence.
Authority competition creates internal selection pressure.
Authority dynamics must preserve boundedness and adaptive stability.
Higher authority should track demonstrated improvements in reachability, correction capacity, and robustness.
Authority changes must alter future computation to be functionally adaptive.
Persistent failure beyond existing mechanism capacity may trigger mechanism-population expansion.
Environment is the final selection pressure on mechanism authority.
Source summarizes commitments: dynamic measurable authority, contradiction-driven attenuation, attribution locality, evidence-gated recovery, and selection over influence.
These are source axioms and constraints and are not presented with empirical validation in this repository.
